analysis.rootCauseHypothesis:
The hosted service likely has a front-end bug or configuration issue in the canvas resize workflow: the canvas size dialog is opening, but the width/height fields are either read-only, immediately overwritten by the current canvas dimensions (456×456), or the Apply Resize handler is not connected to the document model. In other words, the UI accepts the modal interaction but the resize command is not applied to the underlying canvas state, causing the values to revert and preventing the test from continuing. A secondary possibility is that the production build served by the host has stale/corrupted assets or a mismatch between UI and backend APIs so the resize action never reaches the renderer. Underlying error: TEST FAILURE

The required canvas resize could not be applied — width/height inputs revert to the original 456×456 and Apply Resize has no effect, preventing the remainder of the test that depends on a 256×256 canvas.

Observations:
- The Studio loaded and is interactive (Pen tool present and Saved indicator visible), but the canvas reports 456×456 in the UI.
- Multiple attempts to open File → Canvas size…, type 256 for Width and Height, toggle locks, and click Apply Resize resulted in the dialog and canvas still showing 456×456 (typed values did not persist).
- Because the resize cannot be applied, the test steps that require a 256×256 canvas (drawing the stroke in the upper-left quarter, duplicating to 24 frames, exporting APNG and cancelling, and verifying a 256×256 PNG) could not be performed.

recommendedFixTarget.rationale: Investigate and patch the canvas-size modal/state binding in the hosted app. The most likely issue is that the width/height inputs are controlled by app state but are being reset from the current canvas dimensions on each re-render, or the Apply Resize action is wired to a no-op/disabled path in this environment. Ensure the dialog accepts user input, preserves typed values, and dispatches the resize command to the actual document/canvas model. Also verify any save/lock validation logic isn’t rejecting 256×256 and silently reverting to 456×456. If this is behind a reverse proxy or embedded build, check for a broken frontend bundle, feature-flag mismatch, or stale cached assets causing the resize dialog handler to be outdated. A practical fix is to update the resize dialog component so input state is local until Apply, then commit the new dimensions to the canvas/document, trigger a re-render, and persist the change in the project state.
